findings.title: x47.c botnet comes with 18 attack methods, including AI API draining
findings.summary_md: Original disclosure by Qrator Research: x47.c is a previously undocumented Windows botnet advertised by WraithTools with 18 attack methods, credential theft, SOCKS5 proxies, fast-flux C2, and an AI module meant to keep it on infected machines. Publication date of September 23, 2026 is corroborated by same-day Infosecurity Magazine coverage citing Qrator; the Qrator page itself was not directly fetchable due to bot protection.

findings.title: Windows Botnet x47.c Offers AI API Draining, 18 Attack Methods
findings.summary_md: Earliest trade coverage, same day as the Qrator research. Details the AI API drain against OpenAI, xAI, or compatible chat APIs as an OWASP denial-of-wallet attack, and describes an AI Stealth module using xAI's Grok to choose persistence actions including Windows Defender exclusions. Reports an August 3 advertisement pricing the botnet from $200 to $950 and notes Qrator found no test results backing the advertised protection-bypass modes.

findings.title: x47.c Windows Botnet: AI API Credit Draining and 18 Attack Methods Revealed
findings.summary_md: Same-day brief on the Qrator findings, describing x47.c as sold by WraithTools with 18 attack methods and denial-of-wallet tactics that drain paid AI API credits. Confirms the story was in public circulation three days before the story's first-seen timestamp.

findings.title: AI API drain botnet can run up huge bills for victims
findings.summary_md: Cybernews reports that Qrator Labs found x47.c, a Windows botnet package advertising an AI API drain feature in which valid API keys are used to send billable AI requests and exhaust victims' credits. Article date of September 24, 2026 is taken from Cybernews's own X post sharing the piece (page itself is Cloudflare-challenged).

findings.title: New Windows botnet offers AI credit draining and other attack methods
findings.summary_md: SC World brief noting the newly identified x47.c botnet offers 18 attack methods, including one designed to deplete victims' paid AI credits. Published September 24, 2026, two days ahead of the story's first-seen date.
